newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Petrogal to distribute higher sulphur diesel.
newsitem.headline: Petrogal to distribute higher sulphur diesel.

text.p: Portuguese state oil company Petrogal said it would continue to distribute diesel with a higher sulphur content than decreed by the European Union.
According to EU rules, the sulphur content must be reduced to 0.05 percent from 0.2 percent with effect from October 1.

But Petrogal said that the Economy Ministry's Directorate-General for the Environment and Energy had told it that it could continue to distribute diesel with 0.2 percent sulphur while the situation was discussed with the EU.

"The Directorate-General for the Environment and Energy communicate that Petrogal can continue to distribute diesel with 0.2 percent sulphur due to the impossibility of fulfilling the new specifications at this moment," Petrogal said in a statement in English.
It said that the waiver would continue in operation while the "situation is being discussed with European Union managers for this question."

According to Mediterranean oil traders, Portugal and Greece have won more time from the EU to implement the new limits. The traders said that Portugal had until March 1997 and Greece until January 1997.
